questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: ICT is the short form of
questions.explanation: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology: the tools used to create, store, process and share information.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: Which of the following is an ICT tool used mainly for receiving sound broadcasts?
questions.explanation: A radio receives audio broadcasts. A scanner and keyboard are input devices and a projector displays images.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: The correct order of the information processing cycle is
questions.explanation: Data are entered (input), worked on (processing), shown (output) and kept for later use (storage).

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: A teacher records 35 students' marks and the computer works out each student's position in class. The positions are an example of
questions.explanation: Positions are produced by processing the marks, so they are meaningful information.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: Which type of computer is used to forecast the weather because it can perform an extremely large number of calculations very quickly?
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the fastest computers and are used for very heavy calculations such as weather forecasting.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: A computer that works with continuously varying quantities such as temperature or speed, rather than with separate digits, is a(n)
questions.explanation: Analogue computers measure continuous physical quantities. Digital computers work with discrete values (digits).

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: A student in Jos takes part in an online class taught from Lagos. This is an impact of ICT on
questions.explanation: Online lessons (e-learning) are a major contribution of ICT to education.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: Which of the following is a NEGATIVE social effect of ICT?
options: Faster communication between relatives far apart
Spending long hours on social media may reduce face-to-face interaction
Mobile banking reduces the need to carry cash
questions.explanation: Excessive screen time can weaken direct social contact. The other options are benefits of ICT.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: A computer that combines the features of both analogue and digital computers, such as one used in a hospital intensive care unit, is a
questions.explanation: Hybrid computers accept analogue signals (e.g. heartbeat) and process them digitally.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: Mobile phones contribute to economic development mainly by
options: enabling traders to transfer money and find prices quickly
questions.explanation: Mobile money, calls and price information reduce the cost and time of doing business.

questions.stem: The case that contains the motherboard, processor and power supply of a desktop computer is the
questions.explanation: The system unit houses the main internal components of the computer.

questions.stem: Devices connected to the system unit from outside, such as a printer and a mouse, are called
questions.explanation: Peripherals are external devices attached to the computer for input, output or storage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a storage medium?
questions.explanation: A DVD stores data. The mouse is an input device, while the monitor and speaker are output devices.

questions.stem: The main circuit board to which the processor, memory and expansion cards are attached is the
questions.explanation: The motherboard connects all the main internal components and lets them communicate.

questions.stem: Which component supplies power at the correct voltages to the parts inside the system unit?
questions.explanation: The power supply unit converts mains AC to the low DC voltages that the components need.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an output peripheral?
questions.explanation: A projector displays output on a large screen. The others capture input.

questions.stem: A solid state drive (SSD) is preferred to a traditional hard disk drive in many laptops mainly because it
options: loses its data when power is off
has no moving parts, so it is faster and more resistant to shock
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory with no moving parts, so they start faster and withstand knocks better.

questions.stem: A student wants to carry a 2 GB school project between home and school. Which storage medium is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Only the 16 GB flash drive is large enough. 700 MB, 1.44 MB and 512 MB are all less than 2 GB.

questions.stem: Which of these is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is used to enter data. The others produce output.

questions.stem: A set of programs that tells the computer what to do is called
questions.explanation: Software is the collection of programs and instructions that run on the hardware.

questions.stem: Which of the following is application software?
questions.explanation: MS Word helps users carry out a task, so it is application software. Windows, Linux and drivers are system software.

questions.stem: Software whose source code is freely available for anyone to study, change and share is described as
questions.explanation: Open source software makes its source code available under a licence that allows modification and sharing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of open source software?
questions.explanation: LibreOffice is open source. Microsoft Office, Photoshop and CorelDraw are proprietary.

questions.stem: Proprietary software is software that
options: can always be changed freely by any user
has its source code published for everyone
is owned by a company, and users must accept a licence and usually pay for it
questions.explanation: Proprietary software is owned by its developer; users get a licence to use it but not to change or copy it freely.

questions.stem: The main job of system software is to
options: manage the computer's hardware and provide a platform for other programs
questions.explanation: System software, especially the operating system, controls the hardware and allows applications to run.

questions.stem: A small program that lets the operating system communicate with a newly connected printer is a
questions.explanation: A device driver translates the operating system's instructions into commands the particular device understands.

questions.stem: Which statement about open source software is correct?
options: It can never be used in businesses
It is always less secure than proprietary software
It cannot be installed on Windows computers
It may be free of charge, and users can adapt it to their own needs
questions.explanation: Open source software is often free and can be modified. It is widely used by businesses and runs on many platforms.

questions.stem: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Android is an operating system for mobile devices. The others are application programs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a natural threat to computers?
questions.explanation: Floods, earthquakes, lightning and excessive heat are natural threats. Viruses, hacking and theft are human threats.

questions.stem: A program designed to damage files and spread from one computer to another is a
questions.explanation: A virus is malicious code that attaches to files and spreads when they are shared.

questions.stem: Pain in the wrist and fingers caused by long periods of typing with poor posture is called
questions.explanation: Repetitive strain injury (RSI) comes from repeating the same movements for long periods.

questions.stem: Which practice helps to reduce eye strain for a person who uses a computer all day?
options: Sitting very close to the screen
Working in a dark room with a very bright screen
Taking regular breaks and adjusting screen brightness
questions.explanation: Regular breaks, good lighting and correct brightness reduce tiredness of the eyes.

questions.stem: A device that keeps a computer running for a short time during a power cut so that work can be saved is a(n)
questions.explanation: A UPS has a battery that supplies power long enough to save work and shut down properly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of intentional damage to computers by humans?
options: A computer overheating in a hot room
Deliberately smashing a computer during a fight
questions.explanation: Intentional damage is done on purpose by a person. The other examples are natural or accidental.

questions.stem: A worm differs from a virus mainly because a worm
options: can only be spread by floppy disk
spreads by itself over a network without needing a host file
is a type of antivirus program
questions.explanation: A worm is self-replicating and travels across networks on its own; a virus needs a host file and usually human action.

questions.stem: An office in Kano often suffers power surges that damage equipment. The most suitable remedy is to
options: connect the computers through surge protectors or stabilisers
questions.explanation: Surge protectors and voltage stabilisers prevent sudden voltage changes from damaging the hardware.

questions.stem: Back pain among computer users can best be reduced by
options: using an adjustable chair that supports the lower back
placing the monitor on the floor
typing with the keyboard on the lap
sitting on a stool without a backrest
questions.explanation: An ergonomic chair with lumbar support encourages good posture.

questions.stem: Which of these helps to protect a computer from viruses?
questions.explanation: Up-to-date antivirus software detects and removes known malware.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a word processing package?
questions.explanation: MS Word is a word processor. Excel is a spreadsheet, PowerPoint a presentation package and Access a database package.

questions.stem: The flashing vertical line that shows where the next character will appear in a document is the
questions.explanation: The cursor, or insertion point, marks where typed text will appear.

questions.stem: The feature that automatically moves a word to the next line when the current line is full is
questions.explanation: Word wrap moves words to the next line without the user pressing Enter.

questions.stem: Which keyboard shortcut is used to save a document in MS Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves, Ctrl + P prints, Ctrl + V pastes and Ctrl + Z undoes.

questions.stem: To make selected text appear thicker and darker, the user should apply
questions.explanation: Bold makes characters thicker. Italic slants them and underline places a line beneath them.

questions.stem: A typist wants to change every occurrence of "Ibadan" in a long report to "Oyo". The quickest feature to use is
questions.explanation: Find and Replace searches for a word and substitutes another for all occurrences at once.

questions.stem: Text that appears at the top of every page of a document, such as the school's name, is placed in the
questions.explanation: A header repeats at the top of each page; a footer repeats at the bottom.

questions.stem: A typist typed 1050 words in 30 minutes. What is the typing speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = 1050 / 30 = 35 words per minute.

questions.stem: The page orientation in which the page is wider than it is tall is
questions.explanation: Landscape is wider than tall; portrait is taller than wide.

questions.stem: Which command is used to put a copy of the document on paper?
questions.explanation: The Print command sends the document to the printer to produce a hard copy.

questions.stem: In MS Word, which feature should be used to arrange students' names, ages and classes in neat rows and columns?
questions.explanation: A table organises data in rows and columns.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a spreadsheet package?
questions.explanation: Excel is a spreadsheet package used for calculations and charts.

questions.stem: A spreadsheet file in Excel is called a
questions.explanation: An Excel file is a workbook made up of worksheets.

questions.stem: The cell in the fourth column and the seventh row of a worksheet is
questions.explanation: Columns are lettered and rows numbered, so column 4 (D) and row 7 gives D7.

questions.stem: In Excel, every formula must begin with
questions.explanation: Formulas start with = so that Excel knows to calculate rather than display text.

questions.stem: Cells A2 to A6 contain 15, 20, 25, 30 and 10. What value does =MAX(A2:A6) return?
questions.explanation: MAX returns the largest value in the range, which is 30.

questions.stem: Which type of data is the entry "Total Sales" in a worksheet?
questions.explanation: Text entries used as headings are labels; they are not used in calculations.

questions.stem: Cell B3 contains =A3*$C$1. If this formula is copied to B4, the formula in B4 becomes
questions.explanation: $C$1 is an absolute reference and does not change. A3 is relative, so it becomes A4.

questions.stem: Cell A1 contains 8, A2 contains 2 and A3 contains 5. What is the result of =A1+A2*A3?
questions.explanation: Multiplication is done first: 2 x 5 = 10, then 8 + 10 = 18.

questions.stem: A shop owner wants to show what share of total sales each product made. The most suitable chart is a
questions.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a whole.

questions.stem: In a worksheet, rows are identified by
questions.explanation: Rows are numbered 1, 2, 3 and columns are lettered A, B, C.

questions.stem: If C2 contains 4500 and D2 contains 6, which formula gives the total cost in E2?
questions.explanation: =C2*D2 multiplies unit price by quantity. Without the = sign, Excel treats the entry as text.

questions.stem: Which software is mainly used to prepare slides for a talk?
questions.explanation: PowerPoint is a presentation package.

questions.stem: Each page of a presentation is called a
questions.explanation: A presentation is made up of slides.

questions.stem: The feature that applies the same design, fonts and logo to all the slides in a presentation is the
questions.explanation: Changes made on the slide master apply to every slide that uses it.

questions.stem: Which key starts a slide show from the first slide in PowerPoint?
questions.explanation: F5 starts the show from the beginning. F1 opens Help and F7 checks spelling.

questions.stem: Making a picture fly into a slide when the presenter clicks is an example of
questions.explanation: Animation applies movement to objects on a slide. Transitions apply between slides.

questions.stem: The view that shows small images of all slides so they can be rearranged easily is
questions.explanation: Slide Sorter view displays thumbnails for reordering, copying or deleting slides.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best guide for designing slides for a large audience?
options: Fill each slide with long paragraphs
Use few words per slide in a large, clear font
Use many different colours and fonts on each slide
Use very small text so that more fits
questions.explanation: Few words in large, readable fonts keep the audience focused.

questions.stem: Before delivering a presentation, the presenter should FIRST consider
options: the audience and the purpose of the presentation
the colour of the presenter's clothes
questions.explanation: Content, language and length all depend on who the audience is and what the presentation is for.

questions.stem: Printed copies of slides given to the audience to take away are called
questions.explanation: Handouts are printed slide summaries for the audience.

questions.stem: A global network that links millions of computers is the
questions.explanation: The Internet is the worldwide network of networks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a search engine?
questions.explanation: A search engine finds web pages that match keywords.

questions.stem: Copying a file from a website onto your own computer is called
questions.explanation: Downloading copies data from the Internet to your device. Uploading sends data from your device to the Internet.

questions.stem: The part of a browser window where you type the web address is the
questions.explanation: The address bar shows and accepts the URL of the page.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a basic requirement for connecting a computer to the Internet?
options: An Internet service provider and a modem or network connection
questions.explanation: An ISP provides access and a modem, router or network card provides the connection.

questions.stem: Typing a whole message in CAPITAL LETTERS in a chat is considered poor netiquette because it
questions.explanation: In online communication, all capitals is taken as shouting and is impolite.

questions.stem: Which of these is good netiquette when using social media?
options: Sharing other people's photos without permission
Respecting others' views and not posting false information
Posting your friends' phone numbers publicly
questions.explanation: Netiquette means behaving courteously and responsibly online.

questions.stem: To find web pages containing the exact phrase solar energy in Nigeria, a user should type into a search engine
questions.explanation: Putting words in quotation marks asks the search engine for that exact phrase.

questions.stem: A private network that uses Internet technology but is open only to the staff of one organisation is a(n)
questions.explanation: An intranet works like the Internet but is restricted to members of the organisation.

questions.stem: Which of these is a social media platform?
questions.explanation: Facebook is a social media platform. Firefox is a browser and Linux is an operating system.

questions.stem: In the web address https://www.example.com.ng, the part "https" is the
questions.explanation: https is the protocol for secure transfer of web pages. ".ng" is the country code part of the domain.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of ICT. [2 marks]
(b) Describe the information processing cycle. [8 marks]
(c) Discuss five ways in which ICT has improved education in Nigeria. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the use of computers and telecommunication tools to create, process, store, retrieve and share information
2 marks: (b) input: data are collected and entered into the computer
2 marks: (b) processing: the data are worked on (calculated, sorted, compared) according to instructions
2 marks: (b) output: the results are presented as information on screen, paper or sound
2 marks: (b) storage: data and information are saved for future use
10 marks: (c) any five, 2 marks each: e-learning/online classes; access to e-books and research; computer-based tests; school records and result processing; multimedia teaching aids; communication with parents; distance learning
questions.explanation: ICT is the use of computers and communication devices to handle information. The cycle is input, processing, output and storage. ICT has improved education through e-learning, online research, CBT examinations, digital school records, multimedia teaching and distance learning.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three main categories of computer hardware. [3 marks]
(b) Give two examples each of input and output peripherals. [4 marks]
(c) State three components found inside the system unit. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) system unit, peripherals, storage media (1 mark each)
2 marks: (b) any two input devices, e.g. keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone
2 marks: (b) any two output devices, e.g. monitor, printer, speaker, projector
3 marks: (c) any three: motherboard, processor (CPU), RAM, power supply unit, hard disk, expansion cards (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Hardware falls into the system unit, peripherals and storage media. Input: keyboard, mouse. Output: monitor, printer. Inside the system unit are the motherboard, CPU, RAM and power supply.

questions.stem:
(a) Define software. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between system software and application software, giving two examples of each. [8 marks]
(c) (i) Explain the difference between open source and proprietary software. [4 marks]
(ii) State three advantages of open source software to a school. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a set of programs/instructions that tells the computer what to do
2 marks: (b) system software manages the computer hardware and provides a platform for other programs
2 marks: (b) examples of system software: e.g. Windows, Linux, Android, device drivers, utilities
2 marks: (b) application software helps the user to perform specific tasks
2 marks: (b) examples of application software: e.g. MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CorelDraw
2 marks: (c)(i) open source: source code is available and users may study, change and share it
2 marks: (c)(i) proprietary: owned by a company, source code is closed, and use is under a paid licence
6 marks: (c)(ii) any three, 2 marks each: usually free (saves cost); can be adapted to the school's needs; may be installed on many computers legally; community support and updates; reduces piracy
questions.explanation: Software is the set of programs that run on a computer. System software (Windows, Linux) runs the machine; application software (Word, Excel) serves the user's tasks. Open source code is public and modifiable; proprietary software is owned and licensed. Schools gain from low cost, legal installation on many machines, adaptability and community support.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of computer threats. [2 marks]
(b) Give two examples each of natural threats and human threats to computers. [4 marks]
(c) Describe three health hazards associated with the use of computers and state one remedy for each. [9 marks]
(d) State five signs that a computer may be infected with a virus. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) anything that can cause damage to computer hardware, software, data or users
2 marks: (b) natural threats: e.g. flood, fire, earthquake, lightning, excessive heat
2 marks: (b) human threats: e.g. viruses, worms, hacking, theft, intentional damage
3 marks: (c) eye strain - remedy: regular breaks, anti-glare screen, correct brightness
3 marks: (c) back/neck pain - remedy: adjustable chair, monitor at eye level, good posture
3 marks: (c) repetitive strain injury - remedy: wrist support, breaks, correct keyboard height (or electric shock - remedy: proper wiring)
5 marks: (d) any five: slow performance; unexpected pop-ups; files missing or corrupted; programs crashing; strange messages; unusual disk activity; antivirus disabled (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Computer threats are dangers to hardware, software, data and users. Natural threats include floods and lightning; human threats include viruses and theft. Health hazards include eye strain, back pain and RSI, remedied by breaks, ergonomic furniture and correct posture. Virus signs include slowness, pop-ups, missing files and crashes.

questions.stem:
A secretary in Abeokuta has typed a three-page letter in MS Word.
(a) State the steps to save the document with the name ParentsLetter. [3 marks]
(b) Explain how she could change the font of the heading to Arial, size 16. [3 marks]
(c) State four other formatting features available in a word processor. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) click File (or press Ctrl + S) and choose Save/Save As
1 mark: (a) choose the folder (location) and type ParentsLetter in the file name box
1 mark: (a) click Save
1 mark: (b) select (highlight) the heading
1 mark: (b) choose Arial from the font box on the Home tab
1 mark: (b) choose 16 from the font size box
4 marks: (c) any four: bold, italic, underline, alignment/justification, line spacing, bullets and numbering, colour, indentation (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Save: File > Save As, choose a location, type ParentsLetter, click Save. Format: select the heading, pick Arial and size 16 on the Home tab. Other features: bold, italic, underline, alignment, line spacing, bullets.

questions.stem:
The table below shows sales of a small shop in Onitsha entered in Excel:
A1: Item, B1: Unit price (N), C1: Quantity, D1: Amount
A2: Rice (bag), B2: 75000, C2: 3
A3: Beans (bag), B3: 60000, C3: 2
A4: Oil (keg), B4: 42000, C4: 5
(a) Write the formula for D2 and state its value. [3 marks]
(b) Write a formula in D5 to find the total amount and state its value. [4 marks]
(c) State three ways of formatting the worksheet. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) =B2*C2
1 mark: (a) value 225000
2 marks: (b) =SUM(D2:D4)
2 marks: (b) value 555000 (D3 = 120000, D4 = 210000)
3 marks: (c) any three: currency/number format, bold headings, borders, column width, alignment, cell shading (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: D2 =B2*C2 = 225000. D3 = 120000 and D4 = 210000, so D5 =SUM(D2:D4) = 555000. Formatting: currency format, bold headings, borders, column width.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the following spreadsheet terms: (i) cell; (ii) range; (iii) formula; (iv) function. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell references, giving one example of each. [6 marks]
(c) State three uses of spreadsheets in a school. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) cell: the box where a row and a column meet, e.g. B4
2 marks: (a)(ii) range: a group of adjacent cells, e.g. A1:A10
2 marks: (a)(iii) formula: an expression beginning with = that calculates a value, e.g. =A1+A2
2 marks: (a)(iv) function: a built-in formula, e.g. SUM, AVERAGE, MAX
3 marks: (b) relative reference changes when the formula is copied, e.g. A1
3 marks: (b) absolute reference stays fixed when copied, shown with $ signs, e.g. $A$1
6 marks: (c) any three, 2 marks each: computing results and averages; school fees records; budgets; timetables; charts of performance; inventory of equipment
questions.explanation: A cell is a row-column intersection, a range a block of cells, a formula a calculation starting with =, and a function a built-in formula like SUM. Relative references (A1) adjust when copied; absolute references ($A$1) do not. Schools use spreadsheets for results, fees, budgets and charts.

questions.stem:
(a) State three uses of a presentation package. [3 marks]
(b) Outline the steps to insert a picture on a slide in PowerPoint. [3 marks]
(c) Distinguish between slide transition and animation. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) any three: lessons/teaching, business meetings, seminars, product launches, project defence, advertising (1 mark each)
1 mark: (b) select the slide
1 mark: (b) click Insert and then Pictures
1 mark: (b) browse to the picture and click Insert
2 marks: (c) transition: a visual effect when moving from one slide to the next
2 marks: (c) animation: a movement effect applied to an object (text or picture) within a slide
questions.explanation: Presentations are used for teaching, meetings, seminars and marketing. Insert a picture: select the slide, Insert > Pictures, choose the file, Insert. A transition happens between slides; an animation moves an object on a slide.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the Internet. [2 marks]
(b) State four requirements for connecting to the Internet. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the following terms: (i) web browser; (ii) search engine; (iii) uploading. [6 marks]
(d) State four rules of netiquette. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a worldwide network of interconnected computer networks that share information
4 marks: (b) any four: computer or smartphone, modem/router or network card, Internet service provider, browser software, telephone line or data subscription (1 mark each)
2 marks: (c)(i) web browser: software used to open and view web pages, e.g. Chrome, Firefox
2 marks: (c)(ii) search engine: a website that finds information using keywords, e.g. Google, Bing
2 marks: (c)(iii) uploading: sending a file from your device to a computer on the Internet
8 marks: (d) any four, 2 marks each: be polite; do not type in all capitals; respect privacy and copyright; do not spread false information; keep messages brief; do not spam; protect personal information
questions.explanation: The Internet is the global network of networks. Requirements: device, modem/router, ISP, browser, data plan. A browser displays web pages; a search engine finds them; uploading sends files to the Internet. Netiquette includes politeness, no shouting in capitals, respect for privacy and copyright, and no spam or fake news.

questions.stem:
(a) Outline the steps involved in creating an e-mail account. [5 marks]
(b) State three advantages of e-mail over ordinary postal mail. [3 marks]
(c) Give two examples of social media platforms. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) open a browser and go to an e-mail provider site; click Create account/Sign up; fill in name, date of birth and chosen user name; create a password; verify with phone or recovery e-mail and accept the terms (1 mark each)
3 marks: (b) any three: faster delivery; cheaper; can send to many people at once; attachments can be sent; can be read anywhere (1 mark each)
2 marks: (c) any two: Facebook, X (Twitter), Instagram, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, TikTok (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Open the provider's website, choose Create account, enter personal details and user name, set a password, verify and accept terms. E-mail is faster, cheaper, reaches many people and carries attachments. Social media include Facebook and Instagram.
